what_it_does: Modern chip packaging stacks multiple smaller chips (chiplets) on top of each other in three dimensions, connected by thousands of tiny vertical electrical tunnels called Through-Silicon Vias (TSVs). To make sure such a stack does not overheat, engineers run thermal simulations that model heat flow through the structure — but these simulations rely on fine-grained mathematical meshes (grids that divide the geometry into tiny cells) and generating an accurate mesh is computationally expensive and slow. NeuralMesh trains a neural network to predict where the hot spots will be from the chip's geometry, materials, and power maps alone, without running the full iterative simulation first. The network's predictions then guide an automatic process that creates a coarser, faster mesh — fine-grained only in regions the network flagged as thermally critical, and coarser everywhere else. This dramatically cuts the time needed to set up accurate thermal simulations for complex 3D chip packages.
